q1_issues.issue: "a PC" is an indefinite introduced only inside the second Or branch, so its `(Member sk_pc_1 pc)` typing must stay inside that branch; asserting it at top level claims the PC exists regardless of which disjunct holds.
same for "a USB connection" — `(Member sk_usb_1 usb_connection)` is asserted at top level although the entity is posited only by the second disjunct.
the modifier "additional" on "applications" is dropped entirely — no distributed property atom and no fused kind.

the subject is a bare-plural/mass kind under "can", which the instruction set routes to the kind-level reified property rather than an event `(Can e)`; the parse keeps the event form (see the coverage gap — the passive makes the prescribed form inexpressible).

q2_gaps: capability generic in the passive voice ("Ns can be V-ed") — the instruction set routes a kind-level "Ns can V" to `(Inheritance <kind> (can <verb>))`, which cannot express the kind as the undergoer, and offers no alternative form

"via" as a means preposition — it falls under the means test for `Instrument`, but the mechanical rule that the head is "the preposition actually used" leaves it unclear whether `Via` is required instead
notes: The narrow Or-scoping and the distributive split of the coordinated subject both follow the instruction set; the defect is that the second branch's indefinite witnesses escape the branch.
